system.name: Perseus
system.one_liner: a training system that schedules GPU energy consumption across time to remove energy bloat without slowing training

components.name: Perseus Server
components.role: cluster-wide singleton that characterizes the time-energy frontier and caches schedules

components.name: Frontier Characterization
components.role: computes the time-energy tradeoff frontier of an iteration

components.name: Energy Schedule Lookup Table
components.role: caches energy schedules for fast lookup, keyed by target time

components.name: Perseus Client
components.role: framework-integrated, accelerator-specific client that realizes energy schedules

components.name: Asynchronous Frequency Controller
components.role: sets the GPU's frequency during runtime to realize a schedule

components.name: Online Time/Energy Profiler
components.role: profiles pipeline computations online during training

components.name: Distributed Training Framework
components.role: underlying training framework the client integrates with

components.name: GPU
components.role: hardware executing training and reporting profiling/straggler information

content.key_idea: A cluster-wide Perseus Server pre-characterizes the time-energy frontier and caches schedules that a per-job Perseus Client fetches and enforces on GPUs via frequency control, adapting to stragglers.

The server is a cluster-wide singleton.
The client profiles pipeline computations online during training and realizes energy schedules

summary: Perseus reduces energy bloat in large model training by scheduling GPU energy consumption over time without hurting throughput. Figure 4 shows its architecture and workflow as two components connected by a numbered five-step loop. The Perseus Server, a cluster-wide singleton, performs frontier characterization to compute the time-energy tradeoff of a training iteration and caches the resulting schedules in a lookup table (from minimum time Tmin to optimal Topt). The Perseus Client, integrated with the training framework, contains an asynchronous frequency controller and an online time/energy profiler; it requests and applies a schedule from the server, reports profiling information and straggler notifications back, and sets GPU frequencies accordingly. The diagram uses a rounded two-box layout (blue server, green client) with GPUs below the client and circled numbers 1-5 tracing the interaction order.
